knowledge:
- key_parameters: model=specifies the regression model type ("linear", "logistic", "multinomial", "Poisson", "Cox") ;; permutations=number of permutations for calculating permutation-based p-values (default 0 uses asymptotic distribution) ;; standardize=logical indicating whether to standardize covariates to unit variance before testing ;; directional=logical or numeric to direct the test towards alternatives where coefficients have the same sign ;; subsets=a vector or list of vectors specifying subsets of covariates to test ;; weights=a vector or list of weights for the covariates
- alternatives: Likelihood ratio test (LRT) is invariant to parametrization but breaks down in high-dimensional settings where there are more parameters than observations, whereas globaltest remains functional and powerful ;; Competitive gene set enrichment methods (like GSEA or Fisher's exact test) test if a gene set is more associated with the phenotype than random genes, whereas globaltest is a self-contained method testing if any gene in the set is associated
- when_to_use: Use when testing whether a group of many covariates (e.g., gene expression measurements) is associated with a response variable (e.g., clinical phenotype), especially when the number of covariates is much larger than the sample size or when expecting many small effects rather than a few large ones
- pitfalls: The test is not invariant to the parametrization of the alternative model, meaning the choice of contrasts for factor covariates and the scaling of the intercept can alter results ;; Excluding an intercept from the null model makes the test result dependent on the choice of reference category for factors ;; Permutation p-values are only available for the linear model and exchangeable null hypotheses (~1 or ~0) in other models ;; The Shaffer improvement in the inheritance procedure is only valid if the set of covariates at each node is exactly the union of its offspring leaf nodes

workflows.name: covariate_association_and_diagnostics
workflows.intent: Test a group of covariates for association with a response variable and visualize individual covariate and subject contributions.
workflows.stages: 1. Run the global test using gt() ;; 2. Extract test statistics and p-values ;; 3. Generate a hierarchical clustering plot of covariate contributions using covariates() ;; 4. Generate a hierarchical clustering plot of subject contributions using subjects()
workflows.code:
library(globaltest)
gt.options(trace=FALSE, max.print=45)
res <- gt(Y~A, Y~A+B+C, data = X)
p.value(res)
z.score(res)
result(res)
size(res)
covariates(gt(Y,X))
subjects(gt(Y,X))

workflows.name: gene_set_testing
workflows.intent: Test the association of biological pathways (KEGG/GO) with a phenotype using transcriptomic expression data.
input: Golub_Train (ExpressionSet containing gene expression data and phenotype labels)
workflows.stages: 1. Normalize expression data ;; 2. Run pathway-specific global tests using gtKEGG() or gtGO() ;; 3. Extract and plot gene-level features using features()
workflows.code:
library(globaltest)
library(golubEsets)
data(Golub_Train)
library(vsn)
exprs(Golub_Train) <- exprs(vsn2(Golub_Train))
gt(ALL.AML, Golub_Train)
gtKEGG(ALL.AML, Golub_Train, id = "04110")
res <- gtKEGG(ALL.AML, Golub_Train, id = "04110")
features(res, alias=hu6800SYMBOL)

workflows.name: graph_structured_multiple_testing
workflows.intent: Perform multiple testing correction on structured, nested subsets of covariates using Focus Level or Inheritance methods.
workflows.stages: 1. Define the DAG or tree structure of covariate subsets ;; 2. Run focusLevel() or inheritance() to adjust p-values ;; 3. Identify significant leaf nodes using leafNodes() ;; 4. Plot the significant subgraph using draw()
workflows.code:
library(globaltest)
level1 <- as.list(LETTERS[1:10])
names(level1) <- letters[1:10]
level2 <- list(abc = LETTERS[1:3], cde  = LETTERS[3:5], fgh = LETTERS[6:8], hij = LETTERS[8:10])
level3 <- list(all = LETTERS[1:10])
dag <- c(level1, level2, level3)
fl <- findFocus(dag, maxsize=8)
res <- gt(Y,X)
res <- focusLevel(res, sets = dag, focus=fl)
leafNodes(res)
draw(res, names=TRUE)

workflows.name: goodness_of_fit_testing
workflows.intent: Test for non-linearity or missed interactions in a regression model using penalized splines.
input: kyphosis (data frame containing clinical covariates and a binary response)
workflows.stages: 1. Fit a null generalized linear model ;; 2. Test for non-linear effects of covariates using gtPS() ;; 3. Extract the tested smooth terms using sterms()
workflows.code:
library(globaltest)
require("rpart")
data("kyphosis")
fit0<-glm(Kyphosis~., data = kyphosis, family="binomial")
res<-gtPS(fit0)
res@result
sterms(res)
